factual_errors.claim: A transparent RS-485-to-Ethernet converter passes raw bytes only without protocol interpretation, and the PLC never sees a valid DH+ packet
factual_errors.why_wrong: Technically correct at surface level, but dangerously incomplete. MIRA fails to explain that DH-485 requires token-passing arbitration, TX-EN (Transmit Enable) open-collector control line for network coordination, and half-duplex turnaround timing—all of which transparent converters fundamentally cannot provide. The answer focuses on 'missing framing' when the real architectural failures are network arbitration and control signaling.

factual_errors.claim: Suggested troubleshooting steps will diagnose and resolve the communication loss

MIRA buries this solution as a conditional in Step 1 rather than stating it as the definitive answer. A technician might spend hours troubleshooting before discovering the real problem.

factual_errors.claim: No warning about DH-485 voltage specification (0-5V RS-485) vs. Ethernet voltages
